mechanism.summary: A second whole-body register executor, compact_fn::wide, for bodies that read and write named properties, call methods on a receiver, use unary and update operators, read computed elements, and loop where no loop accelerator claims the loop. It supersedes the frozen compact-named-property-access plan, which extended the numeric compact tier's own dispatch loop: measured, carrying the property operations in that loop cost controlflow-recursive 20% whether the extra arms were filtered before the match, kept out of line, or packed into the same eight-byte operation word, so the numeric executor is left byte-identical (its driver symbol is 7360 bytes before and after) and the wide tier has its own operation set, compiler, and frame driver. A body is tried on the numeric tier first and on the wide tier only when the numeric tier declines; the wide set is a superset, so the wide driver runs any admitted callee in a window of its own register stack. Named-property operations delegate to the interpreter's own per-site NamedPropertyCache fast paths and general [[Get]]/[[Set]] fallbacks; register writes are admitted only to the frame's own parameters and hoisted declarations, which the numeric compiler now also requires.
mechanism.generality: Admission is decided solely by the body's bytecode shape (supported opcodes, initialized local slots, agreeing merge depths, no loop a frame-based accelerator has a plan for) and the direct-leaf predicate; it never inspects benchmark names, source paths, property spellings, values, iteration counts or results. The admitted shape -- a constructor or prototype method that reads and writes fields of this and its parameters -- is the shape at the top of the queue: access-binary-trees, cdjs, hash-map, 3d-raytrace and raytrace-public-class-fields all spend 16-35% of their profiles building and dropping the FrameState this tier does not build.
semantic_risks: named reads and writes must follow the interpreter's cache state and fallbacks exactly: getters, setters, Proxies, typed arrays, module namespaces, prototype-resolved methods, read-only and strict-write failures, primitive and null receivers

a callee's this must be seeded from the resolved receiver with the general path's coercion (global object for a sloppy undefined receiver, boxed primitives for sloppy methods, unchanged for strict), and a body reading this is admitted only when a receiver is seeded
loops run by this tier are loops no frame-based accelerator claims, so admitting a body must not take a loop away from the typed, numeric, control or mutation plans
register writes reach only the frame's own bindings; a name resolved from an enclosing scope (global lexical binding, writable captured cell) keeps the general path
errors thrown at any depth of inlined method recursion unwind the wide register stack and propagate to the caller's handler, and recursion past MAX_FRAMES reports a catchable RangeError

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 2,075 main-thread samples, 530 (25.5%) construct a per-activation Vm and its FrameState plus CallEnv for the direct-leaf call path and 257 further samples (12.4%) drop those frames again; the named-property path adds another 200 samples (9.6%). Every TreeNode construction and every itemCheck call pays the full machinery because no compact tier admitted a body that reads or writes a named property; the same shape drives cdjs, hash-map, 3d-raytrace and raytrace-public-class-fields.
